extracted.intended_audience: Heads of executive departments and agencies; agency procurement, logistics, and implementation officials responsible for make-or-buy decisions under OMB Circular A-76
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for federal executive agencies on deciding whether commercial/industrial-type work should be performed in-house by Government personnel or contracted to private sources, including definitions, scope, cost-comparison rules, implementation, and appeals procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy precepts (three-part policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular establishes three equally valid policy precepts: (1) rely on the private sector where private sources are available; (2) retain certain governmental functions in-house because they inherently involve governmental judgment; (3) aim for economy by using rigorous comparative cost analyses when private performance is feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The draft expands the policy statement to recognize governmental functions must be performed by Government personnel and emphasizes comparative cost. It stresses reliance on competitive private enterprise, retention of governmental functions, and rigorous cost comparison to ensure the most economical performance for taxpayers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Government commercial or industrial activity
rubrics_metrics.description: An activity operated and managed by a Federal executive agency that provides a product or service which could be obtained from a private source; must be separable from other functions and be a regularly needed operational activity (not a one-time short-duration project). Includes facility and equipment ownership aspects of GOCO facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A representative (but not comprehensive) listing of such activities is provided in Attachment A. An activity must be separable and regularly needed to be considered under the Circular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Modernization, replacement, upgrade, or expansion of a Government commercial or industrial activity involving additional capital investment of $100,000 or more, or increasing annual operating costs by $200,000 or more, provided the increase exceeds 20% of the total investment or operating cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A consolidation of activities is not an 'expansion' unless the proposed total capital investment or operating cost exceeds the total from individual activities by the amount of the threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: The transfer of work from a Government commercial or industrial activity to performance by a private commercial source under contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: New start
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly-established Government commercial or industrial activity, including a transfer of work from contract to in-house performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Private commercial source
rubrics_metrics.description: A private business or other non-Federal activity, located in the United States, its territories and possessions, the District of Columbia, or Puerto Rico, which provides commercial or industrial product or service required by Government agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Governmental function (must be in‑house)
rubrics_metrics.description: A function which must be performed in‑house due to a special relationship in executing governmental responsibilities, primarily those involving value judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories include (1) discretionary application of Government authorities and program management requiring value judgments (e.g., investigations, prosecutions, direction of national defense, regulatory responsibilities), (2) monetary transactions and entitlements (benefit programs, tax collection, disbursements), and (3) minimum in-house core capabilities in R&D for technical analysis/evaluation and technology base management. Ancillary/support activities are not governmental functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and applicability limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular applies to executive departments and agencies for commercial/industrial activities and replaces prior versions. It does not apply to governmental functions (which must be in-house), and it applies to GOCO facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional limitations: (1) not authority to enter into contracts where no contract authority exists; (2) prohibits contracts that establish an employer-employee relationship between Government and contract personnel (see FPM 300-8 and 300-12); (3) cannot be used to convert solely to meet personnel ceilings or avoid salary limitations (appeal to OMB possible); (4) major system acquisitions governed by Circular A-109; (5) consulting services of a purely advisory nature related to governmental functions are excepted; (6) does not apply to set-aside programs (small business, minority business, Indian preference, Federal prison industries, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of products and services from other Federal agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess property or services available from other Federal agencies should be used in preference to new procurements; when using excess capacity, the performing agency must justify operation of the activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capacity should not be expanded while supporting another agency unless total workload is reviewed and justified under the Circular. Using agency should solicit bids/proposals to establish commercial price when a comparative cost analysis is the basis of decision; agency with excess capacity should prepare the Government cost estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances authorizing Government operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Government operation of a commercial/industrial activity may be authorized only under specified conditions: lack of a satisfactory private source, military necessity (national defense), or favorable relative cost based on comparative cost analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific explanations must be documented; if function was previously contracted, justification must show circumstances are substantially different.

rubrics_metrics.name: No satisfactory commercial source — notification and search requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Before concluding no commercial source is available, the agency must place at least three notices over a 90-day period in the Commerce Business Daily; for urgent requirements publication may be reduced to 30 days with two notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efforts to find sources—especially small and minority-owned businesses—should be supplemented by GSA, SBA, and Department of Commerce assistance. Urgency alone is insufficient; must show commercial sources are not able and Government can provide when needed. Authorization based on disruption requires specific documented explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disruption justification standards
rubrics_metrics.description: When authorization is based on contract performance causing disruption, the disruption must be spelled out in terms of cost, time, and performance measures and shown to be lasting or unacceptable; transitory disruption from conversions is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classified programs, mission basicness, or possibility of strikes are not adequate justification by themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: National defense exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Government may operate activities necessary for combat support, retraining of military personnel, or mobilization readiness; DoD will develop more detailed criteria for such identifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justifications under this exception must show why commercial performance would not meet the military need; DoD/defense agencies to supplement with detailed criteria to be approved by OMB and incorporated into agency instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for comparative cost analysis (relative cost)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions for in-house performance based on economy must be supported by a comparative cost analysis prepared in accordance with the Circular and the Cost Comparison Handbook (supplement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A draft handbook will be published for review. Cost comparison principles are intended to produce greater accuracy and consistency, and will be supplemented by detailed guidance in the handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ground rules for cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Both Government and commercial cost figures must be based on the same scope of work and level of performance; use a precise work statement with performance standards; standard cost factors per handbook; consider all significant Government costs including overhead/indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must defend any costing variations. The base period should be keyed to the expected span of performance to guard against 'buy-in' pricing. Cost comparisons aim at full cost to the maximum extent possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base period, present value, and discounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a base period corresponding to the proposed contract unless circumstances dictate otherwise; use present value analysis and the discount rate prescribed in OMB Circular A-94 when significant differences in capital investment or timing of outlays exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepriced options and recompetition should be used to avoid contract 'buy-in'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold for conducting cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily agencies should not incur the delay and expense of conducting cost comparison studies to justify Government performance for products or services estimated to cost the Government less than $100,000 per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions allowed if there is reason to believe inadequate competition or other factors make commercial prices unreasonable; reasonable efforts must first be made to obtain satisfactory commercial prices and develop competitive sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculating contractor (commercial) costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial cost figures must be based on a firm bid or proposal solicited per procurement regulations. Bidders must be told an in-house cost estimate is being developed and that a contract may or may not result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculating Government operation costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Government cost estimates must assume Government operations are organized and staffed for the most efficient performance; agencies should schedule reviews with internal reorganizations where practical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard cost factors apply. Specific factors: Government retirement cost factor 20.4% (dynamic normal cost projection for Civil Service Retirement), and Federal employee insurance (life and health) benefits cost factor 4% based on actual cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion savings threshold for existing activities
rubrics_metrics.description: An existing in‑house activity may be converted to contract performance on an economic basis only if it will result in savings of at least 10% of the estimated Government personnel costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes a minimum savings requirement to justify conversion from in-house to contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: New start savings threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'new start' (establishing a Government commercial or industrial activity) will not be approved on the basis of economy unless it will result in savings compared to contract performance at least equal to 10% of Government personnel costs plus 25% of equipment and facility costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New starts with capital investment or annual costs of $500,000 or more must be approved by agency head or official at assistant secretary level or equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent review of cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: All cost comparisons must be reviewed by an activity independent of the cost analysis preparer to ensure conformance to the Cost Comparison Handbook instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency implementation responsibilities and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency must designate an official at the assistant secretary level (or equivalent) with overall responsibility for implementation, establish central point(s) of contact for implementation actions, and issue implementing regulations within 60 days identifying designated officials and contact points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central offices must have access to decision documents and data and respond timely to requests concerning inventories, schedules, reviews, and results. Implementing regs and subsequent changes are forwarded to OMB's Office of Federal Procurement Policy for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory, advance scheduling, and notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should prepare advance schedules for review of covered activities and contracts; when proposed expansions exceed thresholds, reviews should be treated as scheduled reviews with at least 60 days given to affected parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If number of activities/contracts is so great that reviews can't be completed in prescribed period, agency may request OMB approval to schedule reviews over a longer period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals / administrative review procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency will establish a procedure for informal administrative review of determinations under the Circular: upon written request by a directly affected party, provide independent, objective review and an expedited determination within 30 days by an official at same or higher level than the initial decision-maker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal procedure provides administrative safeguard (equitable treatment and policy conformance) but does not authorize appeal outside the agency or judicial review. It is intended to protect rights of federal employees, their representatives, contractors and potential contractors; agency decisions under the procedure are final. Appeals cannot be made subject to negotiation, arbitration, or agreements with any one party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract clauses and post-award review/access provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts awarded as a result of reviews under this Circular must contain all applicable clauses related to equal employment opportunities, veterans' preference, minimum wages and fringe benefits, and a provision addressing contractor obligations for subsequent reviews/changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractors must be required to provide information or access needed for subsequent reviews; actions retained in the agency inventory/justification and made available to interested parties upon request to the agency contact point.

rubrics_metrics.name: GOCO (Government-owned, contractor-operated) policy inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Circular applies to operation of GOCO facilities; policies should be incorporated into the make-or-buy procedures of the operating contractor acting as agent of the executive agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of excess capacity and interagency performance guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where services are obtained from another agency, agencies must ensure proper review and consistent treatment; performing agency must justify operation, and excess capacity should not be expanded to support another agency without reviewing total workload under the Circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past inconsistent treatment required separate guidance in the draft to assure proper reviews and avoid activities being listed by both agencies or neither.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment A: illustrative examples of covered activities
rubrics_metrics.description: A representative listing of commercial and industrial activities (e.g., audiovisual services, ADP services, maintenance and repair, manufacturing, real property design/construction/maintenance, medical and dental care, transportation, printing, R&D, office services, security, food services, training, utilities) is provided to illustrate the scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The listing is representative, not comprehensive, and is intended to clarify what types of activities are typically considered commercial/industrial for purposes of the Circular.
